transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, I’m here because everybody keeps acting like I’m making this up, or like I’m just “worked up,” but I know what’s been going on. My wife’s relative came into this house to get at me. That’s the plain truth of it. People can roll their eyes or say things get misplaced, but my tools don’t just move themselves. I know where I put my things—I’ve been working with my hands my whole life, I’m not careless like that.

And it’s not just one thing, you know? If it was one wrench or one weekend, fine, maybe I’d let it go. But my fishing plans keep getting spoiled, again and again, like every weekend something happens, and after months of this you start seeing the pattern. Or I did, anyway. He’s been trying to take over my place, push me out, make me look like I don’t know what I’m talking about. And then everyone acts like I’m the problem for noticing it. That’s why I’m here.
Are you absolutely certain that your wife’s relative has been entering your house to target you?

Yes. I mean, absolutely. I know how that sounds to people, but I’m not guessing here. I’ve lived in my own house long enough to know when something’s off. My tools don’t just move themselves, and they don’t end up where I’d never put them. I’ve been working with tools my whole life — I know my habits, I know my bench, I know where I leave things.

And the fishing, too — that’s not just bad luck every single weekend. Once or twice, sure, anybody can have something go wrong. But month after month? Plans spoiled, things not where they’re supposed to be, the whole thing turning into me looking foolish or unreliable? No. There’s a pattern there.

Everybody keeps acting like I’m imagining it, like I’m worked up or making connections that aren’t there, but I can see it plain as day. My wife’s relative has been coming into this house to get at me. He’s trying to take over my place, push me out, make it seem like I don’t know what I’m talking about. So yes, I’m certain.
Have you been hearing voices when no one else is around?

Voices? No, I don’t think so. I mean, I’m not hearing somebody talking to me when the room is empty, if that’s what you mean. I hear the normal things anybody hears — the house settling, a car outside, maybe noises at night that make you stop and listen — but not voices, not like some person speaking when there’s no one there.

And I want to be clear, because people keep trying to turn this into something it isn’t. This isn’t about me hearing things. It’s about what’s actually been happening. But no, I haven’t noticed voices or anything like that.
Have you had any recent illness or injury involving your brain or nerves?

I don’t know of anything like that. I mean, I haven’t had some big head injury or anything involving my brain that I’m aware of. No doctor has told me, “This is a nerve problem,” if that’s what you’re asking.

I get why you have to ask, but I don’t really think that’s what this is. I’ve worked assembly and fabrication a long time, so sure, you bump yourself here and there over the years, but nothing I’d call a brain injury. Nothing recent that stands out to me.
Has anyone told you that your speech or your thoughts seem disorganized or hard to follow?

Disorganized? I don’t know. Nobody’s said it to me like that, not in those words. I mean, people say I “go on” about things, or that I repeat myself, especially when I’m trying to explain something important, but that’s not the same as being hard to follow. At least I don’t think it is.

I try to be clear. Sometimes I have to give the whole background because if I leave out one part, then people act like the thing I’m saying doesn’t make sense. So I start at the beginning, and then maybe I explain too much, but that’s because I’m trying to make sure it’s understood properly. If someone doesn’t follow me, I’d rather they just ask instead of making it sound like my thoughts are all mixed up.

So no, not really. I haven’t had anyone tell me my speech is disorganized. Maybe they get impatient with me, but I don’t think that means I’m not making sense.
Have you had a period recently where you felt unusually high, energetic, or elated?

Unusually high or elated? No, I wouldn’t say that. I mean, I have days where I’m more wound up, sure, especially if I’m trying to deal with something or explain myself and people aren’t listening, but that’s not the same as being “high” or overly happy.

I haven’t been walking around feeling on top of the world or like I’ve got some endless energy for no reason. Mostly I just feel like I’m trying to keep up with what’s going on. Maybe I get tense or focused, and maybe I talk more when I’m trying to make a point, but I wouldn’t call it elated. That word doesn’t really fit.
Has your wife’s relative ever gotten into your house in a way that seemed impossible, like without using a door or window?

I don’t know about “impossible” like you mean floating through a wall or something. I’m not saying that. But I know he’s been getting into the house somehow, because things don’t just happen on their own.

My tools will be in one place and then they’re somewhere else, or something I need is missing right when I need it. And my fishing plans—almost every weekend, something gets messed up. That’s not just bad luck every single time. After months of it, you start seeing the pattern. He’s trying to get at me, trying to make it so I look disorganized or like I can’t keep my own place straight.

Everybody keeps acting like I’m imagining it, and that’s part of why I’m here, but I know what I’ve seen in my own house. He wants to take over my place, push me out, make it like I don’t belong there anymore. I can’t tell you exactly how he gets in every time, but I know he’s been in there.
Before all this started, have you generally been a person who often suspects that other people are trying to harm, cheat, or deceive you?

Before all this? I don’t know. I mean, I’ve never thought of myself as someone who goes around suspecting everybody of things. I’m not naïve, you know, I think you have to be careful with people—at work, with money, with what people say versus what they actually do—but I don’t think that’s the same as believing everyone is out to harm me.

I’ve had situations where I didn’t trust someone, sure. Everybody has. If someone gives you a reason, then you pay attention. But I wouldn’t say I was always thinking people were trying to cheat me or deceive me before all this. Not as a general thing. I mostly just did my job, came home, kept to myself, handled my own business.

So… no, not really. I don’t think that was me, not in the way you’re asking.
How long has this been going on?

It’s been about nine months now, give or take. It started after my wife’s relative moved into the house. Before that, things weren’t like this—not in this way.

I remember because when he first came in, I was trying to be reasonable about it, you know, trying not to make a big issue right away. But then over time, things started happening, and it kept building. So if you’re asking how long I’ve been dealing with all of this, I’d say around nine months, from when he moved in.
Since this started, have you had trouble keeping up with your usual work or daily responsibilities?

No, not in the main way, I guess. I mean, I still get up and go to the plant. I still do my assembler work. I punch in, I do what I’m supposed to do, I get through the day. Nobody’s paying my bills for me—I keep those paid, I keep myself fed, I wash up, I take care of what I have to take care of.

It’s not like I’m just lying in bed all day or forgetting how to function. That’s not what this is. The problem is at home, with him, with my things being moved or messed with. That’s where all the trouble is centered. Once I’m away from the house, I can mostly keep my routine, but then I come back and I’m dealing with all that again, and it wears on you. But work and basic responsibilities, I’m still handling those.
Have you ever felt that your thoughts were being controlled or put into your mind by someone else?

No… I don’t think so. I mean, I have my own thoughts, if that’s what you’re asking. They might go around and around in my head sometimes, and I can get stuck thinking about things more than I’d like, but it doesn’t feel like somebody is putting them there.

Controlled… no, that sounds different from what I experience. I’ve never had the feeling like there’s some outside force steering my mind or making me think certain words. My thoughts feel like mine, even when I’m upset or when I can’t stop turning something over in my head.

I’m not sure if I’m answering exactly the way you mean it, but no, I haven’t noticed anything like someone controlling my thoughts or planting thoughts in my head.
Aside from your wife’s relative entering the house and interfering with your things, have you had any other strong beliefs that others say are untrue?

Other strong beliefs… I mean, it all ties back to him, really. I’m not walking around thinking every person in town is against me, if that’s what you mean. But this thing at home—people keep telling me I’m making too much of it, or that I’m imagining it, and I’m not. I know what I see.

My tools don’t just move themselves. I keep them a certain way. I’ve worked with my hands long enough to know where I put things. Then I come back and they’re not where I left them, or something’s off, and everyone acts like I’m supposed to believe it’s nothing. Same with my fishing plans. It’s like every time I’m trying to have one simple weekend, something happens that ruins it, and after months of it you start seeing the pattern.

So no, it’s not a bunch of different beliefs, but I do believe he came into that house to get at me. He’s been trying to take over my place, make me look foolish, push me out little by little. People can say that’s not true, but they’re not the ones living there and watching it happen.
Have you found yourself becoming less interested in people or activities you used to care about?

I don’t know… not exactly. I still care about the things I’ve always cared about, I think. I mean, I still like fishing. I still think about going, getting my gear together, having a quiet morning where nobody’s bothering me. That hasn’t gone away.

People, though… I guess I’m a little more careful with people now, maybe less eager to sit around and make small talk. But I wouldn’t say I stopped caring about everyone or everything. I still go to work, I still talk when I need to, I still have things I want to do. It’s more that I get worn down, and then I don’t always feel like being around folks or pretending everything’s fine.

So if you mean have I lost interest completely, no, I wouldn’t put it that way. I’ve just been preoccupied, I guess, and that can make other things harder to enjoy the same way.
Have you been drinking heavily lately?

Heavily? I don’t know what you’d call heavy. I have a drink sometimes, sure, like a lot of people do, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been drinking heavily lately. Not like sitting around all day with a bottle or anything like that.

I mean, if I’m stressed or wound up, I might have something to take the edge off, but I don’t think alcohol is the issue here. I haven’t really been keeping count, to be honest. Maybe that sounds vague, but I just haven’t thought of it that way. So… no, not heavily, at least not as far as I’d describe it.
Have you recently cut down on alcohol after a period of drinking more than usual?

Cut down? I’m not sure I’d describe it that way. I mean, I haven’t been tracking it like some kind of logbook, so it’s hard for me to say, “Yes, I was drinking this much and now I’m drinking that much.”

There have been days where maybe I had more than I should’ve, especially if I was tense, but I don’t know that there was a whole period of drinking more than usual and then I deliberately cut back. It’s more… some days I might have a drink, some days I don’t. I haven’t really thought of it as a pattern.

So I guess the honest answer is I’m not sure. I don’t think I’ve recently made some big effort to cut down, if that’s what you mean.
Have you ever seen someone or something that other people there could not see?

Seen something nobody else could see? I mean… not really, no. At least not in the way I think you’re asking, like seeing a person standing there that everyone else says isn’t there, or some object in the room that only I can see. I can’t say that’s happened.

Sometimes you catch something out of the corner of your eye, you know, like a shadow moves or headlights go by or your mind fills in a shape for a second, but then you look and it’s just a coat or a reflection or whatever. I think that happens to everybody, especially when you’re tired or tense. But I wouldn’t call that seeing things.

So, no… I haven’t had some clear experience where I was seeing someone or something and other people right there couldn’t see it.
Did this start suddenly, over a day or two?

No, not suddenly like over a day or two. It’s been going on a while now… about nine months, I’d say. It really seemed to start after my wife’s relative moved into our home. That’s when things changed, at least from how I remember it.

It wasn’t like I woke up one morning and everything was different all at once. It was more like… after they came into the house, over time, it just became this thing that was there, and it’s been going on since then. So, no, not a couple of days. More like months. Nine months or so.
Have you become less emotionally expressive than you used to—for example, do people say your face or voice seems flat?

I don’t know… I haven’t really thought about it in those terms. I mean, nobody has sat me down and said, “Your face is flat,” or “You sound flat,” not like that.

I suppose if I’m tired or irritated or trying not to get pulled into something, I might not show much on my face. But that’s not the same as being unable to express emotion, right? I still feel things. I still get upset, I still laugh if something’s actually funny, I still react.

Maybe some people might think I’m quieter or more guarded sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’ve noticed my voice going flat or my face not moving. It’s not something I’ve been keeping track of. So… no, not that I’m aware of.
Have you ever felt that the television, radio, or casual remarks from other people were sending special messages meant specifically for you?

No, not really like the TV or radio, no. I don’t sit there thinking the news anchor is talking in code to me or anything like that. Casual remarks… I mean, people say things, and sometimes you know there’s a meaning behind it, but I wouldn’t put it the way you said it.

What I’m saying is more direct than that. I’m here because everybody keeps acting like I’m imagining it or making too much of it, but I know what’s been happening in my own house. My wife’s relative came in there and started getting at me, little by little. My tools don’t just move themselves. Things I keep in certain places, that I know I put away right, are suddenly not where they should be. And then I’m supposed to believe it’s just me forgetting? No.

And my fishing plans—every weekend it seems like something gets spoiled, something comes up, or there’s interference right when I’m trying to have one thing for myself. That doesn’t happen by accident over and over for months. After all this time, it’s plain to me he’s trying to take over my place, make me look like the problem, and push me out. So, not messages from the television, no. It’s what’s happening around me.
Do you believe your wife’s relative has any special powers or unusual methods that let him get into the house or move your things?

Special powers? No, I’m not saying he’s got some magic ability or anything like that. I’m not talking about him walking through walls or using some kind of… I don’t know, device. That’s not what I mean.

What I’m saying is he’s in the house, he has access, and he knows exactly what he’s doing. People keep trying to make it sound like I’m imagining it, but I know where I put my tools. I’ve worked with my hands my whole life—I know when something’s been moved. They don’t just wander off by themselves.

And the fishing, too. Every time I try to make plans, somehow it gets spoiled or interfered with. Once or twice, fine, maybe that’s life. But over and over, weekend after weekend? After months of that, you start seeing the pattern. Plain as day to me, he’s trying to get at me, take over my place in my own home, make me look like the unreasonable one, and push me out. So no, I’m not saying “special powers.” I’m saying he’s doing it on purpose.

doctor.question: Since this started, have you had trouble keeping up with your usual work or daily responsibilities?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 1
target_item.manifestation: I still get up, go to the plant, do my assembler work, keep the bills paid, and take care of myself like I always have. The trouble is all centered on what’s happening in my house with him and my things.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the symptoms have interfered with usual work or daily responsibilities, which directly concerns overall functioning being preserved aside from the delusion's impact.

patient.answer:
No, not in the main way, I guess. I mean, I still get up and go to the plant. I still do my assembler work. I punch in, I do what I’m supposed to do, I get through the day. Nobody’s paying my bills for me—I keep those paid, I keep myself fed, I wash up, I take care of what I have to take care of.

It’s not like I’m just lying in bed all day or forgetting how to function. That’s not what this is. The problem is at home, with him, with my things being moved or messed with. That’s where all the trouble is centered. Once I’m away from the house, I can mostly keep my routine, but then I come back and I’m dealing with all that again, and it wears on you. But work and basic responsibilities, I’m still handling those.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the delusional belief is non-bizarre and isolated versus accompanied by additional schizophrenic symptoms, to distinguish delusional disorder from schizophrenia-spectrum acute/transient psychosis.
doctor.question: Have you ever felt that your thoughts were being controlled or put into your mind by someone else?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about thought control or thought insertion, which is not covered by the provided symptom profiles. The available delusions profile concerns fixed beliefs about the wife's relative interfering with his belongings and home, not thoughts being controlled or inserted.

patient.answer:
No… I don’t think so. I mean, I have my own thoughts, if that’s what you’re asking. They might go around and around in my head sometimes, and I can get stuck thinking about things more than I’d like, but it doesn’t feel like somebody is putting them there.

Controlled… no, that sounds different from what I experience. I’ve never had the feeling like there’s some outside force steering my mind or making me think certain words. My thoughts feel like mine, even when I’m upset or when I can’t stop turning something over in my head.

I’m not sure if I’m answering exactly the way you mean it, but no, I haven’t noticed anything like someone controlling my thoughts or planting thoughts in my head.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the persecutory delusion is non-bizarre and isolated without broader schizophrenia-spectrum features, which would help distinguish delusional disorder from schizophrenia or acute/transient psychosis.
doctor.question: Aside from your wife’s relative entering the house and interfering with your things, have you had any other strong beliefs that others say are untrue?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because everybody keeps acting like I’m imagining it, but I know my wife’s relative came into this house to get at me—my tools don’t move themselves, my fishing plans don’t get spoiled by accident every weekend, and after all these months I can see plain as day he’s been trying to take over my place and push me out.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about whether there are any additional strong fixed beliefs that others say are untrue, which directly concerns delusions.

patient.answer:
Other strong beliefs… I mean, it all ties back to him, really. I’m not walking around thinking every person in town is against me, if that’s what you mean. But this thing at home—people keep telling me I’m making too much of it, or that I’m imagining it, and I’m not. I know what I see.

My tools don’t just move themselves. I keep them a certain way. I’ve worked with my hands long enough to know where I put things. Then I come back and they’re not where I left them, or something’s off, and everyone acts like I’m supposed to believe it’s nothing. Same with my fishing plans. It’s like every time I’m trying to have one simple weekend, something happens that ruins it, and after months of it you start seeing the pattern.

So no, it’s not a bunch of different beliefs, but I do believe he came into that house to get at me. He’s been trying to take over my place, make me look foolish, push me out little by little. People can say that’s not true, but they’re not the ones living there and watching it happen.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are prominent negative symptoms, which would support schizophrenia over delusional or acute psychotic disorder.
doctor.question: Have you found yourself becoming less interested in people or activities you used to care about?

target_item.reason: The question asks about reduced interest in people or previously enjoyed activities, which is not covered by the provided symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
I don’t know… not exactly. I still care about the things I’ve always cared about, I think. I mean, I still like fishing. I still think about going, getting my gear together, having a quiet morning where nobody’s bothering me. That hasn’t gone away.

People, though… I guess I’m a little more careful with people now, maybe less eager to sit around and make small talk. But I wouldn’t say I stopped caring about everyone or everything. I still go to work, I still talk when I need to, I still have things I want to do. It’s more that I get worn down, and then I don’t always feel like being around folks or pretending everything’s fine.

So if you mean have I lost interest completely, no, I wouldn’t put it that way. I’ve just been preoccupied, I guess, and that can make other things harder to enjoy the same way.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there is a plausible medical or substance-related cause for the delusion, especially alcohol-related cognitive impairment that could support an organic delusional disorder rather than primary delusional disorder or schizophrenia-spectrum illness.
doctor.question: Have you been drinking heavily lately?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about heavy alcohol use, but the provided symptom profile does not include substance or alcohol use.

patient.answer:
Heavily? I don’t know what you’d call heavy. I have a drink sometimes, sure, like a lot of people do, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been drinking heavily lately. Not like sitting around all day with a bottle or anything like that.

I mean, if I’m stressed or wound up, I might have something to take the edge off, but I don’t think alcohol is the issue here. I haven’t really been keeping count, to be honest. Maybe that sounds vague, but I just haven’t thought of it that way. So… no, not heavily, at least not as far as I’d describe it.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there is a plausible substance-related cause, especially alcohol withdrawal hallucinosis/paranoia, to distinguish an acute/substance-induced psychosis from a primary delusional disorder.
doctor.question: Have you recently cut down on alcohol after a period of drinking more than usual?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about recent alcohol reduction after heavier drinking, but the provided symptom profiles do not include alcohol use or withdrawal-related symptoms.

patient.answer:
Cut down? I’m not sure I’d describe it that way. I mean, I haven’t been tracking it like some kind of logbook, so it’s hard for me to say, “Yes, I was drinking this much and now I’m drinking that much.”

There have been days where maybe I had more than I should’ve, especially if I was tense, but I don’t know that there was a whole period of drinking more than usual and then I deliberately cut back. It’s more… some days I might have a drink, some days I don’t. I haven’t really thought of it as a pattern.

So I guess the honest answer is I’m not sure. I don’t think I’ve recently made some big effort to cut down, if that’s what you mean.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there is clear evidence of persistent hallucinations, which would favor schizophrenia or organic psychosis over a delusional disorder.
doctor.question: Have you ever seen someone or something that other people there could not see?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about visual hallucinations—seeing things others cannot see—which is not covered by the provided symptom profile focused on delusions, functioning, impairment, or duration.

patient.answer:
Seen something nobody else could see? I mean… not really, no. At least not in the way I think you’re asking, like seeing a person standing there that everyone else says isn’t there, or some object in the room that only I can see. I can’t say that’s happened.

Sometimes you catch something out of the corner of your eye, you know, like a shadow moves or headlights go by or your mind fills in a shape for a second, but then you look and it’s just a coat or a reflection or whatever. I think that happens to everybody, especially when you’re tired or tense. But I wouldn’t call that seeing things.

So, no… I haven’t had some clear experience where I was seeing someone or something and other people right there couldn’t see it.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has been an abrupt onset of psychotic symptoms, which would help distinguish acute transient psychotic disorder from persistent delusional disorder or schizophrenia.
doctor.question: Did this start suddenly, over a day or two?

target_item.name: Duration
target_item.manifestation: This has been going on for about nine months, ever since my wife’s relative moved into our home.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the time course/onset of the symptoms, which is covered by the duration profile.

patient.answer:
No, not suddenly like over a day or two. It’s been going on a while now… about nine months, I’d say. It really seemed to start after my wife’s relative moved into our home. That’s when things changed, at least from how I remember it.

It wasn’t like I woke up one morning and everything was different all at once. It was more like… after they came into the house, over time, it just became this thing that was there, and it’s been going on since then. So, no, not a couple of days. More like months. Nine months or so.

inference.note: F23.3 ruled out because onset was not acute (symptoms developed over ~9 months rather than within 2 weeks). Persistent non-bizarre persecutory delusion with preserved functioning and no hallucinations, thought insertion, disorganization, negative symptoms, mania, or clear organic trigger makes F22 most likely; F20.0, F06.2, and F60.0 remain differential considerations.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are prominent negative symptoms, which would help distinguish schizophrenia from delusional disorder, organic psychosis, and paranoid personality disorder.
doctor.question: Have you become less emotionally expressive than you used to—for example, do people say your face or voice seems flat?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about reduced emotional expression or flat affect, which is not covered by the provided symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
I don’t know… I haven’t really thought about it in those terms. I mean, nobody has sat me down and said, “Your face is flat,” or “You sound flat,” not like that.

I suppose if I’m tired or irritated or trying not to get pulled into something, I might not show much on my face. But that’s not the same as being unable to express emotion, right? I still feel things. I still get upset, I still laugh if something’s actually funny, I still react.

Maybe some people might think I’m quieter or more guarded sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’ve noticed my voice going flat or my face not moving. It’s not something I’ve been keeping track of. So… no, not that I’m aware of.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there is a non-bizarre delusional belief without other core schizophrenic symptoms, which would favor delusional disorder over schizophrenia or paranoid personality disorder.
doctor.question: Have you ever felt that the television, radio, or casual remarks from other people were sending special messages meant specifically for you?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because everybody keeps acting like I’m imagining it, but I know my wife’s relative came into this house to get at me—my tools don’t move themselves, my fishing plans don’t get spoiled by accident every weekend, and after all these months I can see plain as day he’s been trying to take over my place and push me out.
target_item.reason: The question is asking about possible delusional beliefs, specifically ideas of reference such as TV, radio, or remarks sending special messages meant for the patient.

patient.answer:
No, not really like the TV or radio, no. I don’t sit there thinking the news anchor is talking in code to me or anything like that. Casual remarks… I mean, people say things, and sometimes you know there’s a meaning behind it, but I wouldn’t put it the way you said it.

What I’m saying is more direct than that. I’m here because everybody keeps acting like I’m imagining it or making too much of it, but I know what’s been happening in my own house. My wife’s relative came in there and started getting at me, little by little. My tools don’t just move themselves. Things I keep in certain places, that I know I put away right, are suddenly not where they should be. And then I’m supposed to believe it’s just me forgetting? No.

And my fishing plans—every weekend it seems like something gets spoiled, something comes up, or there’s interference right when I’m trying to have one thing for myself. That doesn’t happen by accident over and over for months. After all this time, it’s plain to me he’s trying to take over my place, make me look like the problem, and push me out. So, not messages from the television, no. It’s what’s happening around me.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the fixed persecutory belief is culturally implausible/bizarre enough to favor schizophrenia over delusional disorder or paranoid personality traits.
doctor.question: Do you believe your wife’s relative has any special powers or unusual methods that let him get into the house or move your things?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because everybody keeps acting like I’m imagining it, but I know my wife’s relative came into this house to get at me—my tools don’t move themselves, my fishing plans don’t get spoiled by accident every weekend, and after all these months I can see plain as day he’s been trying to take over my place and push me out.
target_item.reason: The question is probing the nature and extent of the fixed belief about the wife’s relative moving things or getting into the house, including whether the belief involves unusual or impossible methods.

patient.answer:
Special powers? No, I’m not saying he’s got some magic ability or anything like that. I’m not talking about him walking through walls or using some kind of… I don’t know, device. That’s not what I mean.

What I’m saying is he’s in the house, he has access, and he knows exactly what he’s doing. People keep trying to make it sound like I’m imagining it, but I know where I put my tools. I’ve worked with my hands my whole life—I know when something’s been moved. They don’t just wander off by themselves.

And the fishing, too. Every time I try to make plans, somehow it gets spoiled or interfered with. Once or twice, fine, maybe that’s life. But over and over, weekend after weekend? After months of that, you start seeing the pattern. Plain as day to me, he’s trying to get at me, take over my place in my own home, make me look like the unreasonable one, and push me out. So no, I’m not saying “special powers.” I’m saying he’s doing it on purpose.

opening_question.intent: Elicit the patient's chief complaint in their own words to begin the diagnostic interview
opening_question.question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a single, persistent persecutory delusional belief lasting about 9 months that his wife's relative is entering the house, moving tools, sabotaging fishing plans, and trying to push him out. He is firmly convinced despite others disputing it. There are no confirmed hallucinations, thought insertion/control, bizarre delusions, disorganized speech, negative symptoms, manic symptoms, or significant functional decline outside the delusional theme. No neurological illness/injury is reported. This pattern is most consistent with persistent delusional disorder, persecutory type.
